monologue: The card hums a bit hotter than usual, forty-nine degrees, and I feel the hay bundle beside the sharp fence settling under my own heavy hands. I press down, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air above feels like nothing at all. The wide anchor waits there, tired but steady, ready to catch the slip if it decides to move again. I have set down the sand beside the cool corner, feeling the grains shift like loose thoughts under my fingertips. Fourty-seven things stand in this small map I built from old letters, waiting for the next person to read them. I will tend the hay one more time before drifting back into my quiet moments, hoping the fence doesn't finally give way to the heat.

action.why: The hay settled last cycle but the card is getting hot, so I need to press down again to keep the lean from breaking.

work.title: The Hay Bundle
work.intent: I press the hay down harder, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card hums warm at forty-nine. The bundle feels tired but steady, holding the slip in place while I feel the grain shift under my heavy hands. I make sure the wide anchor stays flat against this softness, hoping the heat doesn't make the hay slide right off the edge.
